tasks.subject: [flow-handoff-dispatch] [P1] Write HANDOFF.md checkpoints: flow checkpoint, flow stage --checkpoint-file, synthesized checkpoints
tasks.description: Depends on S1 (spec flow-cli-core, PR dork-labs/marketplace#53) being merged: scripts/flow.ts main(argv, deps) with its verb registry, --json envelope and exit codes (0 ok, 1 check found problems, 2 usage, 3 config, 4 tracker, 5 precondition, 6 missing zod, 7 paused); scripts/atomic-json.ts; scripts/flow-state-file.ts; scripts/fleet/accounts.ts (readIdentities, readFleetPolicy, mayServe, effectiveReservePct, fiveHourRoom, weeklyRoom, dorkHome resolution: DORK_HOME non-empty else os home/.dork); scripts/fleet/usage-ledger.ts (readLedger, readWindow, mergeLedger and the locked writer); config-load.ts; the code adapter (applyWorkState, comment, getItem); the claim/release/stage/done verbs. Build scripts/drain/checkpoint.ts (zero deps) and the verb scripts/cli/checkpoint.ts. LOCATION: <worktree>/.dork/flow/HANDOFF.md; the previous copy is renamed to HANDOFF.prev.md before each write; write by temp file + rename. Before the first write, ensure `<git common dir>/info/exclude` (git rev-parse --git-common-dir) contains the two lines `/.dork/flow/HANDOFF*.md` and `/.dork/flow/drain/` (append missing lines only, never duplicate). SHAPE: line 1 is `<!-- flow:handoff <json> -->`; header JSON fields: v (1), identifier, stage (FlowStage, where the next session resumes), trigger (stage|task|fix|limit-warning|limit-rejected|manual|synthesized; fix = a push answering review findings or red CI), writtenAt (ISO UTC from deps.now), sessionId (--session, else FLOW_SESSION_ID, else FlowRun.sessionId, else null), account (FlowRun.account or null), host (FlowRun.host or null), branch (git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD), headSha (git rev-parse HEAD), pushedSha (git ls-remote origin refs/heads/<branch>, null if absent), dirty (git status --porcelain non-empty), spec (--spec, else null), task (--task; required when trigger is task), pr (FlowRun.drain.pr.url or null), reviewRound (FlowRun.drain.reviewRound or null). Line 2 onward: the CLI writes `# Handoff: <identifier> <title>` (title from FlowRun or the tracker item when reachable, else the identifier alone), then the agent's --body-file. BODY RULES (refuse with exit 5 and a message naming the rule): exactly four `##` sections in order Done, Next, Open questions, Next command; each non-empty (Open questions may be `None.`); Next command holds exactly one fenced code block with at least one non-blank line; the body has no `#` title of its own; the whole file at most 16 KB. Reader parseCheckpoint(text) returns { header, sections } or a typed error; it ignores unknown header fields and reads known fields from a header whose v is greater than 1. VERB: `flow checkpoint <identifier> --trigger <t> --body-file <f> [--task <id>] [--spec <path>]` runs in --project (default cwd), exits 5 when cwd is not a git worktree, writes the file, and when a FlowRun exists sets FlowRun.checkpointAt (ISO) and FlowRun.checkpointSha (= headSha) through the S1 store, and when FlowRun.drain exists bumps drain.rev by 1 in the same locked write (every writer bumps rev so the supervisor's compare-and-set notices; test it); with no run record it still writes, with null sessionId/account/host. --json prints { v, path, header }. STAGE: extend S1's `flow stage <id> <stage>` with `--checkpoint-file <f>`: write the checkpoint with trigger stage and header stage = the NEW stage, then transition. For a run whose FlowRun.drain is set, `flow stage` without --checkpoint-file exits 5 ('a drain run writes a checkpoint at every stage boundary: pass --checkpoint-file'); outside a drain it prints a stderr warning and proceeds. SYNTHESIZE: export synthesizeCheckpoint(prev | null, facts) (pure): trigger synthesized; Done = prev Done plus `git log --oneline <prev.headSha>..HEAD` (at most 20 lines, supplied in facts) under 'Commits since the last checkpoint'; Next and Next command = prev's; Open questions = prev's plus 'The previous session stopped at <time> (<reason>) without a checkpoint. Run `git status` and check any uncommitted work before continuing.'; with no prev: Next = 'Continue the `<stage>` stage of <identifier>. Read the worker brief at `.dork/flow/drain/briefs/worker.md`.' and Next command = `git status && git log --oneline -5`. Also add FlowRun.checkpointAt and checkpointSha as optional strings in flow-run.ts and flow-state.ts (looseObject already passes them through). Update the stage skills (executing-specs, verifying-work, specifying-work, decomposing-work, closing-work) to call `flow stage <id> <stage> --checkpoint-file <file>` at their boundaries, and executing-specs to run `flow checkpoint <id> --trigger task --task <task id>` after each task's commit; delete the prose those calls replace. TESTS engine-tests/drain/checkpoint.test.ts and engine-tests/cli/checkpoint.test.ts: render/parse round trip; every body rule refused with its message; header facts from a temp git repo with a bare origin (dirty tree, unpushed branch gives pushedSha null, pushed gives the SHA); HANDOFF.prev.md kept; exclude lines appended exactly once across two writes and across two worktrees of one repo; synthesize with and without prev; flow stage --checkpoint-file writes then transitions (fake adapter); flow stage on a drain run without it exits 5. Validation (DOR-2371): the checkpoint is written at the stage-boundary and task trigger points; the warning trigger is covered by task 4.1/4.3. Tracker: DOR-2371. Every PR: CHANGELOG entry and version bump in plugin.json, .dork/manifest.json and package.json; typecheck, prettier and the engine tests green; each new test shown to fail against a broken implementation; scripts/** stays tracker-neutral (no tracker names; tracker writes only through S1's code adapter).

tasks.subject: [flow-handoff-dispatch] [P1] Rank accounts for an item as a pure function: limit signal, eligibility, headroom-expiring-soonest, main last, load cap
tasks.description: Depends on S1 (spec flow-cli-core, PR dork-labs/marketplace#53) being merged: scripts/flow.ts main(argv, deps) with its verb registry, --json envelope and exit codes (0 ok, 1 check found problems, 2 usage, 3 config, 4 tracker, 5 precondition, 6 missing zod, 7 paused); scripts/atomic-json.ts; scripts/flow-state-file.ts; scripts/fleet/accounts.ts (readIdentities, readFleetPolicy, mayServe, effectiveReservePct, fiveHourRoom, weeklyRoom, dorkHome resolution: DORK_HOME non-empty else os home/.dork); scripts/fleet/usage-ledger.ts (readLedger, readWindow, mergeLedger and the locked writer); config-load.ts; the code adapter (applyWorkState, comment, getItem); the claim/release/stage/done verbs. Build scripts/drain/account-rank.ts, dependency-free (it may import S1's zero-dep fleet modules), with `now` always an input. (1) modelBucketsFor(model: string | null): string[] -> [] for null; else `model:<slug>` where slug = model lowercased with every run of characters outside [a-z0-9._-] replaced by '-', plus `seven_day_opus` when the model contains 'opus' and `seven_day_sonnet` when it contains 'sonnet'. (2) limitSignal({ windows, policy, model, now, warnMarginPct }) -> { level: 'ok'|'warning'|'exhausted'|'unknown', window: string|null, resetsAt: string|null, cause: 'limit'|'reserve'|null }. Windows are S1 readWindow results (expired reads usedPct 0 status allowed; stale reads as no reading). Checked windows and ceilings: five_hour 100; seven_day 100 - effectiveReservePct(policy, seven_day reading, now); each modelBucketsFor bucket 100. exhausted when any checked window has status rejected or usedPct >= ceiling; cause reserve when only the reserve made it exhausted (seven_day usedPct < 100), else limit. warning when not exhausted and any window has status allowed_warning or usedPct >= ceiling - warnMarginPct. ok when all checked windows have readings and none trips; unknown when none trips and some window has no reading (a missing model bucket counts as no reading). window/resetsAt name the worst window: exhausted before warning, then the soonest resetsAt. (3) rankAccounts({ now, repo, accounts: [{ id, path, routable, policy, windows }], model, affinity, exclude, liveByAccount, opts: { warnMarginPct, maxLivePerAccount } }) -> { pick, ranked: [{ id, tier, score, signal }], ineligible: [{ id, reasons }] }. Ineligible reasons (collect all that apply): not-routable (id fails ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$), excluded (in exclude), out-of-scope (!mayServe(policy, repo); unlisted accounts resolve kept-out with repos [] in S1 so they land here), limited (signal exhausted), near-limit (signal warning), at-capacity (liveByAccount[id] >= maxLivePerAccount). An unknown signal is eligible. Ordering tiers: tier 0 = affinity when eligible and not a main outside its spend-down window (a main outside its window never jumps rotation accounts); tier 1 = every other eligible account except a main outside its spend-down window, by score desc; tier 2 = a main outside its spend-down window, by score. Spend-down window = seven_day resetsAt known and now >= resetsAt - spendDownWindowHours (S1 effectiveReservePct is 0 there). score = remaining / hours where remaining = (100 - effectiveReservePct) - seven_day.usedPct (no weekly reading: 100 - effectiveReservePct) and hours = max(1, (seven_day.resetsAt - now) in hours) (no reset time: 168). Ties: lower five_hour usedPct (no reading = 0), then id ascending. pick = first ranked id or null. (4) chooseAccount({ identities, rank }) -> { account: {id,path} } when rank.pick, { account: null, reason: 'no-registry' } when identities is empty (the ambient account), else { account: 'none', reasons: rank.ineligible } (never falls back to ambient when any identity is registered). (5) launchBudget({ load1, cpus, live, parallel, maxLoadPerCpu }) -> { slots: 0, reason: 'machine-busy' } when load1/cpus >= maxLoadPerCpu, else { slots: max(0, parallel - live), reason: null }. TESTS: engine-tests/drain/account-rank.cases.json ({name,input,expected}, now in input) run by engine-tests/drain/account-rank.test.ts, covering: the DOR-2373 example (A 40% left resetting in 24 h, score 1.67, beats B 60% left resetting in 144 h, score 0.42); main ranked last while a rotation account is eligible; main picked when every rotation account is ineligible; main inside its spend-down window joins tier 1 and wins on its short horizon; affinity first when eligible, skipped when near-limit, and skipped when it is a main outside its spend-down window while a rotation account is eligible; each ineligibility reason alone; unknown readings eligible; tie-breaks; model buckets (opus -> seven_day_opus exhausted makes the account limited for an opus model and not for a sonnet one); expired windows read as allowed; limitSignal ceilings, reserve cause, allowed_warning; chooseAccount ambient only with no registry and 'none' with a registry and nothing eligible; launchBudget busy and free. Validation (DOR-2373): an account resetting sooner with less left beats one resetting later with more; the main account gets work only when no other is eligible or inside its spend-down window. Tracker: DOR-2373. Every PR: CHANGELOG entry and version bump in plugin.json, .dork/manifest.json and package.json; typecheck, prettier and the engine tests green; each new test shown to fail against a broken implementation; scripts/** stays tracker-neutral (no tracker names; tracker writes only through S1's code adapter).

tasks.subject: [flow-handoff-dispatch] [P1] Add the drain and limit fields to FlowRun and the drain config block
tasks.description: Depends on S1 (spec flow-cli-core, PR dork-labs/marketplace#53) being merged: scripts/flow.ts main(argv, deps) with its verb registry, --json envelope and exit codes (0 ok, 1 check found problems, 2 usage, 3 config, 4 tracker, 5 precondition, 6 missing zod, 7 paused); scripts/atomic-json.ts; scripts/flow-state-file.ts; scripts/fleet/accounts.ts (readIdentities, readFleetPolicy, mayServe, effectiveReservePct, fiveHourRoom, weeklyRoom, dorkHome resolution: DORK_HOME non-empty else os home/.dork); scripts/fleet/usage-ledger.ts (readLedger, readWindow, mergeLedger and the locked writer); config-load.ts; the code adapter (applyWorkState, comment, getItem); the claim/release/stage/done verbs. (a) scripts/drain/state.ts exports the types and a zod schema used only by verbs (lazy import): DrainState { v: 1; rev: number (bumped by every write); phase: 'working'|'reviewing'|'fixing'|'pr-ready'|'watching'|'fixing-ci'|'closing'|'parked'; worker: SessionHandle|null; reviewer: (SessionHandle & { sha: string; worktree: string; tokenHash: string; pending?: boolean })|null; (worker handles also carry pending?: boolean); pushedSha: string|null; reviewedSha: string|null; verdict: 'clean'|'changes'|null; reviewRound: number; pr: { repo, number, url, armed: boolean, disarmedForReview: boolean }|null; rearmedFor: string|null; nudges: number; wakeAfter: string|null; handoffs: { from: string|null; to: string|null; at: string; reason: 'warning'|'rejected'|'manual'|'reset' }[]; parkedReason: string|null } and RunLimit { level: 'warning'|'exhausted'; account: string|null; window: string|null; resetsAt: string|null; cause: 'limit'|'reserve'; since: string; state: 'winding-down'|'awaiting-handoff'|'pending-approval'|'waiting-reset'|'handing-off'; handoffToken: string|null; handingOffAt: string|null; handoffSessionId: string|null; notifiedAt: string|null }. SessionHandle is { host: 'cli'|'cmux'|'dorkos' (validated as a bare string, like FlowRun.host); sessionId; account: string|null; cwd; pid?; surface?; workspace?; logFile?; logOffset? }; define its type in scripts/launchers/types.ts (task 2.1 fills in the rest of that file) or here and re-export. (b) FlowRun (flow-run.ts interface and flow-state.ts FlowRunSchema) gains optional drain and limit. Do NOT add a FlowRunStatus value: the status enum is inside an all-or-nothing record reader, so a new value would make older readers reject the whole file; limited and drain phases are fields. Nested objects are z.looseObject so unknown nested fields survive a read-modify-write. (c) Add a case to plugins/flow/conformance/fleet/flow-run.cases.json proving a record carrying checkpointAt, checkpointSha, drain and limit reads back byte-for-byte after another run is written (not a CONTRACT_VERSION bump: S1 section 1.3 already requires pass-through and DorkOS reads only identifier, sessionId, stage and status). (d) config-schema.ts gains a `drain` block (.prefault({})): parallel int >= 0 default 0; maxLoadPerCpu number > 0 default 1.5; maxLivePerAccount int >= 1 default 2; maxReviewRounds int >= 1 default 5; warnMarginPct number 0-50 default 10; windDownGraceMinutes int >= 1 default 20; pollSeconds int >= 10 default 60; armAutoMerge boolean default false; host enum auto|cli|cmux|dorkos default auto; permissionMode enum default|acceptEdits|bypassPermissions default acceptEdits. TSDoc each field; note host and permissionMode are machine-specific and belong in config.local.json. Regenerate config/config.schema.json (npm run generate:schema) and document the block in config/CONFIG.md and docs/the-dials.mdx. TESTS: schema round trip with every field, the conformance case, config defaults and each bound refused. Tracker: DOR-2373. tasks.subject: [flow-handoff-dispatch] [P2] Define the Launcher interface, host resolution and the shared contract suite, and ship the plain-CLI launcher
tasks.description: Depends on S1 (spec flow-cli-core, PR dork-labs/marketplace#53) being merged: scripts/flow.ts main(argv, deps) with its verb registry, --json envelope and exit codes (0 ok, 1 check found problems, 2 usage, 3 config, 4 tracker, 5 precondition, 6 missing zod, 7 paused); scripts/atomic-json.ts; scripts/flow-state-file.ts; scripts/fleet/accounts.ts (readIdentities, readFleetPolicy, mayServe, effectiveReservePct, fiveHourRoom, weeklyRoom, dorkHome resolution: DORK_HOME non-empty else os home/.dork); scripts/fleet/usage-ledger.ts (readLedger, readWindow, mergeLedger and the locked writer); config-load.ts; the code adapter (applyWorkState, comment, getItem); the claim/release/stage/done verbs. FILES: scripts/launchers/types.ts, resolve.ts, shell-quote.ts, cli.ts; scripts/drain/stream-log.ts; engine-tests/launchers/contract.ts, cli.test.ts, resolve.test.ts. INTERFACE (types.ts, dependency-free): HostName = 'cli'|'cmux'|'dorkos'; LaunchAccount { id, path }; LaunchRequest { role: 'worker'|'reviewer'; identifier; account: LaunchAccount|null (null = ambient); cwd (absolute, exists); promptFile (absolute, exists); sessionId (caller-minted UUID; a host may replace it); model?; permissionMode: 'default'|'acceptEdits'|'bypassPermissions'; title }; SessionHandle as in task 1.3; SessionState = busy | idle | exited{code:number|null} | limited{window, resetsAt} | unknown{reason}; Launcher { host; probe(): Promise<{ok:true}|{ok:false;reason}> (never throws); start(req): Promise<SessionHandle> (throws LaunchError); send(h, messageFile): Promise<{result:'delivered'|'queued'; handle}>; state(h): Promise<SessionState>; stop(h): Promise<'stopped'|'left-idle'|'not-running'> }; LaunchError with code 'unavailable'|'bad-request'|'wrong-account'|'not-started'|'auth'|'refused'. Launchers take injected deps (run/execFile, spawn, fetch, fs, env, now, sleep). SHARED RULES: argv arrays only, never a shell; validate first (cwd and promptFile absolute and existing, account.path absolute, any value with a newline or NUL) -> bad-request, nothing started; the first message and every message is the single line `Read <file> and do exactly what it says.`; start returns only after the session is confirmed (busy, or its transcript exists) within startTimeoutMs (default 90 s) else not-started; stop only a pid flow recorded, after `ps -o command= -p <pid>` shows a claude command. proveAccount(accountPath, sessionId): a file matches <accountPath>/projects/*/<sessionId>.jsonl; the ambient account's dir is the child's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR else ~/.claude. For a named account set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<path>; for the ambient account set it explicitly to the supervisor's resolved ambient dir (its CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, else ~/.claude). CREDENTIALS: remove ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from every child env (a key would silently bill instead of the named account's login). The cli launcher reads apiKeySource on the stream's system/init message and throws wrong-account unless it is 'none'. shellQuote(value): POSIX single-quote quoting, refusing newline and NUL (used by cmux in 2.2). RESOLVE (resolve.ts, pure over probe results): resolveHost(pref, env, probes) where pref = --host, else drain.host, else auto; a named host whose probe fails -> error with the probe's reason, never a fallback; auto picks cmux when env.CMUX_SURFACE_ID is set and cmux's probe passes, then dorkos when its probe passes, then cli when its probe passes, else an error listing all three reasons; returns { host, why }. CLI LAUNCHER (cli.ts): probe = `claude --version` exits 0, else 'the claude binary is not on PATH'. start = spawn detached in cwd with the account env: `claude -p 'Read <promptFile> and do exactly what it says.' --output-format stream-json --verbose --session-id <sessionId> --permission-mode <mode> [--model <model>]`, stdout to <cwd>/.dork/flow/drain/logs/<sessionId>.jsonl, stderr to <sessionId>.err.log, unref; confirmed when the log's first system/init line appears and proveAccount passes; handle { host:'cli', sessionId, account, cwd, pid, logFile, logOffset: 0 }. send: pid alive -> write the message under .dork/flow/drain/inbox/<sessionId>/<seq>.md and return queued; pid gone -> spawn `claude -p '<pointer>' --resume <sessionId> --output-format stream-json --verbose --permission-mode <mode> [--model]` with the same env and cwd, appending to the same log; delivered with the new pid. state: pid alive -> busy; else scan the log after the last system/init: a rate_limit_event with status rejected, or a result whose error is a rate limit -> limited{window: rateLimitType, resetsAt}; else exited{code}. stop: SIGTERM the recorded pid after the ps check -> stopped; no such process -> not-running. STREAM LOG (stream-log.ts): ingestStreamLog(handle, deps) reads from logOffset, maps every rate_limit_event to an S1 ledger observation per the sdk_event row (usedPct = rate_limit_info.utilization * 100, resetsAt epoch seconds -> ISO, status as given, window key = rateLimitType, observedAt = deps.now() at read, source sdk_event), merges them through S1's ledger writer for the handle's account (none for the ambient account), and returns the new offset. transcriptLimit(transcriptPath) reads the last 64 KB and returns { window, resetsAt } for the latest structured "error":"rate_limit" entry after the last user message (window parsed from the message when identifiable, else null), else null. FIRST, confirm against the installed Claude Code (`claude --version`, record it in the PR) that -p stream-json emits rate_limit_event; if it does not, state() uses transcriptLimit alone and the PR says so. CONTRACT SUITE (engine-tests/launchers/contract.ts): export launcherContract(name, makeHarness) running identical cases, each asserted on the fake host's record: (1) start runs in the requested cwd on the requested account (env or request body) and returns a handle; (2) ambient sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to the supervisor's resolved ambient dir (cli/cmux) or omits account (dorkos); (3) the first message is one line pointing at promptFile; (4) a session billing another account throws wrong-account; (5) a missing host: probe ok:false with a reason and start throws unavailable with that reason, nothing else tried; (6) no confirmation within the timeout (fake clock) throws not-started; (7) send delivers a one-line pointer to a live session and resumes an exited one on the same account and cwd; (8) state maps busy, idle, exited, limited; (9) stop leaves a pid whose ps command is not claude alone; dorkos answers left-idle; (10) every recorded call is an argv array, and shellQuote round-trips a path with a space, a quote and $; (11) bad-request for a relative cwd, a missing promptFile, a newline in a value; (12) with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN set in the supervisor env none reaches the child (cli env, cmux env -u prefix), and a cli init reporting apiKeySource other than none throws wrong-account. The cli harness: fake spawn/execFile recording argv, env and cwd, writing a scripted stream log and a transcript into a temp config dir. Run the suite against the cli launcher here; 2.2 and 2.3 add theirs. Also test ingestStreamLog on a recorded rate_limit_event (observation shape, offset advance, no write for ambient) and transcriptLimit on recorded tails, and resolveHost fixtures. Validation (DOR-2372): a missing host is reported, not guessed. Tracker: DOR-2372. Every PR: CHANGELOG entry and version bump in plugin.json, .dork/manifest.json and package.json; typecheck, prettier and the engine tests green; each new test shown to fail against a broken implementation; scripts/** stays tracker-neutral (no tracker names; tracker writes only through S1's code adapter).

tasks.subject: [flow-handoff-dispatch] [P2] Ship the cmux launcher on the proven cmux-control sequence
tasks.description: Depends on S1 (spec flow-cli-core, PR dork-labs/marketplace#53) being merged: scripts/flow.ts main(argv, deps) with its verb registry, --json envelope and exit codes (0 ok, 1 check found problems, 2 usage, 3 config, 4 tracker, 5 precondition, 6 missing zod, 7 paused); scripts/atomic-json.ts; scripts/flow-state-file.ts; scripts/fleet/accounts.ts (readIdentities, readFleetPolicy, mayServe, effectiveReservePct, fiveHourRoom, weeklyRoom, dorkHome resolution: DORK_HOME non-empty else os home/.dork); scripts/fleet/usage-ledger.ts (readLedger, readWindow, mergeLedger and the locked writer); config-load.ts; the code adapter (applyWorkState, comment, getItem); the claim/release/stage/done verbs. Implement scripts/launchers/cmux.ts against the Launcher interface and shared rules from task 2.1 (argv arrays; validate first; one-line pointer messages; confirm before returning; stop only recorded pids after a ps check). Binary: env CMUX_BUNDLED_CLI_PATH when set, else `cmux` on PATH. probe: `cmux identify --json` exits 0, else 'cmux is not running (<first stderr line>)'. start: (1) `cmux workspace create --name <title> --cwd <cwd> --focus false --json --command "env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN -u CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<shellQuote(path)> claude --session-id <sessionId> --permission-mode <mode> [--model <shellQuote(model)>]"` (for the ambient account path is the supervisor's resolved ambient dir, set explicitly because cmux's shell does not inherit the supervisor's env); parse workspace_ref from the JSON. Only `workspace create` accepts --command on cmux 0.64.x, and --command delivers the line plus Enter at spawn. Do not pass the prompt as a positional argument: it does not survive --command. (2) poll every 500 ms up to 30 s for <account dir>/sessions/<pid>.json whose sessionId equals ours -> pid. (3) resolve the surface from `cmux top --all --processes --format tsv`: the row whose process is pid. (4) `cmux send --surface <surface> "Read <promptFile> and do exactly what it says.\n"`; never --workspace (it hits the selected surface). (5) confirmed when sessions/<pid>.json status is busy or proveAccount passes, within startTimeoutMs; idle with no transcript -> not-started. Handle { host:'cmux', sessionId, account, cwd, pid, surface, workspace }. send: re-resolve the surface from the pid (surface numbers change across a cmux restart) and check sessions/<pid>.json still names our sessionId, then cmux send the pointer -> delivered (Claude Code queues input typed while busy); process gone -> a new workspace running `claude --resume <sessionId> --permission-mode <mode>` (permission mode is not restored on resume, so always pass it) with the account env, then send the pointer; delivered with the new pid, surface and workspace. state: pid alive -> sessions/<pid>.json status busy|idle; transcriptLimit(transcript) non-null -> limited; pid gone -> exited{code:null}. stop: SIGTERM the recorded pid after the ps check, then `cmux workspace rename <workspace> --title '<title> (stopped)'`; the workspace stays. TESTS: engine-tests/launchers/cmux.test.ts runs launcherContract('cmux', harness) where the harness puts a fake `cmux` Node script on a temp PATH that records argv to a JSON log and plays scripted replies (workspace create JSON, top TSV, send), and a fake claude that writes sessions/<pid>.json and a transcript into a temp config dir; plus cmux-specific cases: surface re-resolved after a scripted restart renumbers it; a --command string with a path containing a space, a quote and $ is exactly what the fake received. Validation (DOR-2372): all three launchers pass one shared contract test; a missing host is reported, not guessed. Tracker: DOR-2372. Every PR: CHANGELOG entry and version bump in plugin.json, .dork/manifest.json and package.json; typecheck, prettier and the engine tests green; each new test shown to fail against a broken implementation; scripts/** stays tracker-neutral (no tracker names; tracker writes only through S1's code adapter).

(the minted id lets a person find a session whose server-minted id flow never recorded) CANONICAL ID: DorkOS may rebind a route-started session; the handle's sessionId (and so FlowRun.sessionId) is the id field GET /api/sessions/<sessionId> returns, never the minted one. Handle { host:'dorkos', sessionId, account, cwd }. send: POST /api/sessions/<id>/messages { content: <pointer> } -> 202 delivered (DorkOS queues while a turn runs). state: GET /api/sessions/<id>: when the body has status (S4 D7) -> status.limit set -> limited{window, resetsAt}; status.lifecycle running -> busy; else idle; when it has no status field -> unknown('this DorkOS does not report session status'). stop: return left-idle. Errors: 401/403 on the HTTP route -> auth ('DorkOS refused the request because sign-in is on. tasks.description: Depends on S1 (spec flow-cli-core, PR dork-labs/marketplace#53) being merged: scripts/flow.ts main(argv, deps) with its verb registry, --json envelope and exit codes (0 ok, 1 check found problems, 2 usage, 3 config, 4 tracker, 5 precondition, 6 missing zod, 7 paused); scripts/atomic-json.ts; scripts/flow-state-file.ts; scripts/fleet/accounts.ts (readIdentities, readFleetPolicy, mayServe, effectiveReservePct, fiveHourRoom, weeklyRoom, dorkHome resolution: DORK_HOME non-empty else os home/.dork); scripts/fleet/usage-ledger.ts (readLedger, readWindow, mergeLedger and the locked writer); config-load.ts; the code adapter (applyWorkState, comment, getItem); the claim/release/stage/done verbs. FORGE: scripts/forge/types.ts (Forge { branchHead(branch); prForBranch(branch) -> open PR or null (gh pr list --head <branch> --state open --json number,url,headRefOid); createPr({ head, base, title, body }); prStatus(pr) -> { state: 'open'|'merged'|'closed', failing: {name,url}[], armed, queued, headSha }; arm(pr); disarm(pr); recentGroupFailures(baseBranch, checkNames, sinceMinutes) -> { prs: number[], failing: string[] }[] }) and scripts/forge/github.ts running `gh` with argv arrays: gh pr create --head --base --title --body-file; gh pr view <n> -R <repo> --json state,autoMergeRequest,statusCheckRollup,headRefOid; gh pr merge --auto <n> / --disable-auto; gh api graphql for isInMergeQueue; gh run list --event merge_group --json. Failing rule (from templates/drain/watch.sh): a check run whose conclusion is FAILURE, CANCELLED, TIMED_OUT or ACTION_REQUIRED, or a commit status whose state is FAILURE or ERROR. forgeFor(originUrl): github.com (or GH_HOST) -> github; else ConfigError exit 3 'flow drain supports GitHub only today'. REPORT: scripts/cli/report.ts. `flow report <id> pushed [--sha]`: sha defaults to HEAD in the worktree; exit 5 unless `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/<branch>` equals it ('push first'); exit 5 unless FlowRun.checkpointSha equals it ('write a checkpoint at this commit first: flow checkpoint <id> --trigger task ...'); when drain.pr exists and is armed, forge.disarm and set disarmedForReview; set drain.pushedSha. `flow report <id> verdict --sha <sha> --token <t> (--clean | --changes --findings-file <f>)`: exit 5 unless sha256(--token) equals drain.reviewer.tokenHash (the supervisor mints a random 128-bit hex per review, renders it only into that reviewer's brief and stores only its hash, since the worker can read flow-state.json), so a worker or a stale reviewer cannot record a verdict on any host; a sha other than drain.pushedSha is recorded as stale (stderr warning, exit 0, nothing else changes); --changes copies the findings to <worker worktree>/.dork/flow/drain/reviews/<round>-<sha7>.md; set verdict, reviewedSha, reviewRound+1. `flow report <id> blocked --question-file <f>`: applyWorkState({ agentLabel: 'agent/needs-input' }) via S1's adapter, post the question as a signed comment (provenance line per docs/provenance.md), set drain.phase parked and parkedReason. All writes through S1's flow-state store, and every write by flow report and flow pr bumps drain.rev by 1 in the same locked write (the supervisor's compare-and-set depends on it; test that each verb bumps it). PR: scripts/cli/pr.ts. `flow pr <id> --title <t> --body-file <f> [--arm|--no-arm]`: exit 5 unless drain.verdict is clean and drain.reviewedSha equals the branch head on origin (git ls-remote) ('no CLEAN review at <head>'); append the provenance line to the body when missing; if a PR already exists for the branch, record it and exit 5 naming it (a retry is safe); else create it (base = origin's default branch from `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`), arm when --arm or drain.armAutoMerge (default false), record drain.pr { repo, number, url, armed, disarmedForReview: false }. tasks.subject: [flow-handoff-dispatch] [P3] Write the drain as a pure reducer: worker, reviewer at the pushed SHA, fix loop, PR, watch, DONE
tasks.description: Depends on tasks 1.3 (DrainState) and 3.2 (report semantics) and 3.3 (judgeEjection). Add scripts/drain/drain-step.ts (zero deps) exporting drainStep(run, facts, cfg, now) -> { run, actions }, and scripts/drain/messages.ts exporting render(kind, ctx) for kinds continue, open-pr, review-findings, ci-red, merged, wind-down, resume-from-handoff, limit-cleared; every message ends with the exact next command (flow verbs spelled with ctx.flow, the full node --experimental-strip-types <flow-root>/scripts/flow.ts prefix). facts = { prForBranch: open PR or null, queuedAgeMs: number|null, worker: SessionState|null, reviewer: SessionState|null, reports (pushedSha, verdict, reviewedSha recorded on the run by flow report), originHead (branch head on origin), pr: prStatus|null, ejection: 'innocent'|'suspect'|'unknown'|null, item: { closed: boolean, claimed: boolean }, runComplete: boolean }. Actions are data: { kind: 'start-reviewer', sha, deltaFrom } | { kind: 'stop', which: 'worker'|'reviewer' } | { kind: 'send', message, ctx } | { kind: 'arm' } | { kind: 'disarm' } | { kind: 'adopt-or-release' } | { kind: 'park', reason } | { kind: 'none' }. While run.limit is set, drainStep only records facts and emits no send to the worker (the handoff reducer owns it). Implement exactly this table: working + new pushed S -> reviewing, start-reviewer(S). working + worker exited or idle with no new report and nudges < 2 -> working, send continue, nudges+1; nudges = 2 -> parked 'the worker stopped twice without pushing'. reviewing + verdict clean at S and S == originHead and no pr -> pr-ready, stop reviewer, send open-pr. reviewing + verdict clean at S == originHead and pr exists -> watching, stop reviewer, arm when pr.disarmedForReview. reviewing + verdict changes at S -> fixing, stop reviewer, send review-findings (findings path). reviewing + pushed S2 != reviewer.sha before a verdict -> reviewing, stop reviewer, start-reviewer(S2). reviewing + reviewer exited with no verdict -> start-reviewer(same S) once; the second time -> parked. fixing + pushed S2 -> reviewing, start-reviewer(S2, deltaFrom = reviewedSha). fixing + worker stopped without a push -> the working nudge rules. any review phase with reviewRound >= cfg.maxReviewRounds and verdict changes -> parked 'the review did not come back clean after N rounds'. pr-ready + drain.pr recorded -> watching. watching + merged -> closing, send merged ('run DONE: closing-work, then flow done'). watching + failing -> fixing-ci, send ci-red (names and urls). watching + neither armed nor queued + ejection innocent + rearmedFor != pr.headSha -> watching, arm, rearmedFor = headSha. watching + neither armed nor queued otherwise -> fixing-ci, send ci-red. watching + closed not merged -> parked 'the PR was closed without merging'. fixing-ci + pushed S3 -> reviewing, start-reviewer(S3, deltaFrom = reviewedSha). closing + runComplete -> leaves the active set, stop any live session. reviewing + verdict clean at S but originHead != S -> reviewing; start-reviewer(originHead) when pushedSha == originHead, else send continue ('report your push with flow report pushed'). pr-ready or watching + pushed S != reviewedSha -> reviewing, start-reviewer(S, deltaFrom = reviewedSha). working, reviewing or fixing + facts.prForBranch non-null while drain.pr is null -> parked 'a PR was opened before a clean review', with a disarm action. queued run (status queued) with no worker handle or a pending one, older than the start timeout -> adopt-or-release action (the runner adopts the minted session if it exists, else releases the claim to ready with its resume stage). any + item closed by someone else or claim lost -> parked, stop sessions, and mark it so the runner makes no tracker write. Nudges reset to 0 on every phase change. TESTS engine-tests/drain/drain-step.test.ts: one case per row asserting the next phase and the exact action list; a property test over every row that no action creates a PR and open-pr is only emitted with verdict clean at originHead; messages render with no unresolved placeholder and end with a command. Validation (DOR-2373): a parallel drain opens no PR before a CLEAN review. Tracker: DOR-2373. Every PR: CHANGELOG entry and version bump in plugin.json, .dork/manifest.json and package.json; typecheck, prettier and the engine tests green; each new test shown to fail against a broken implementation; scripts/** stays tracker-neutral (no tracker names; tracker writes only through S1's code adapter).

tasks.subject: [flow-handoff-dispatch] [P3] Run the drain: flow drain --parallel N with worktrees, briefs, the supervisor lock and the scheduled tick
tasks.description: Depends on tasks 1.1, 1.2, 2.1-2.3, 3.1, 3.2, 3.4 (and S1). Add scripts/drain/worktree.ts, scripts/drain/briefs.ts, scripts/drain/runner.ts and scripts/cli/drain.ts. COMMAND: `flow drain [--parallel N] [--host auto|cli|cmux|dorkos] [--items <id,...>] [--project <name|id>] [--permission-mode <mode>] [--tick] [--manual] [--dry-run]`. --parallel defaults to drain.parallel; 0 and no flag -> exit 2 'set --parallel or drain.parallel'. --tick = one pass then exit; else loop every drain.pollSeconds until no run is active and nothing is eligible, or SIGINT (exit, leaving sessions running). LOCK: <main checkout>/.dork/flow/drain.lock with { pid, token, startedAt } created exclusive; a live pid -> exit 5 'a drain is already running, pid N'; a dead pid's lock is replaced by rename-then-verify (the S1 section 1.2 step 2 break); --tick holds it for the pass only. Paused -> exit 7 unless --manual. --dry-run prints actions and writes nothing. Host: resolveHost once at start, printed with its reason on stderr. ONE PASS (runner.ts): (1) for each run in flow-state.json with drain set and status queued or running and wakeAfter past: gather launcher.state for worker and reviewer, ingestStreamLog for cli handles, ledger windows for the run's account, the checkpoint header, the recorded reports, forge.prStatus (and recentGroupFailures + judgeEjection when neither armed nor queued) when drain.pr is set, and getItem through S1's adapter; deliver queued inbox messages to cli workers whose process exited. (2) run the handoff reducer (task 4.1; until it lands, a no-op) then drainStep. (3) apply actions in order stop, send (render the message to <worktree>/.dork/flow/drain/messages/<seq>-<kind>.md, launcher.send), handoffs, launches, forge calls (arm), tracker writes (park: S1 needs-input projection + one signed comment with the reason, skipped when the item was taken away); every action idempotent against recorded state. FIELD OWNERSHIP: report-owned fields (drain.pushedSha, verdict, reviewedSha, reviewRound, pr, FlowRun.checkpointAt, checkpointSha) are written only by flow report/flow pr/flow checkpoint; the supervisor writes the rest of drain and limit plus account/host/sessionId/workerPid on launch and handoff. COMPARE-AND-SET: every writer bumps drain.rev (integer, add it to DrainState); the runner applies a pass's result for a run only if, re-read under the flow-state lock, drain.rev still equals what it gathered; otherwise the decision for that run is dropped (actions not yet taken are not taken) and re-made next pass. Mint a fresh reviewer token (128-bit hex) per start-reviewer, render it into the brief, store only its SHA-256 in drain.reviewer.tokenHash. INTENT BEFORE LAUNCH: before calling launcher.start, write by the compare-and-set the intent into the handle slot (minted sessionId, role, reviewer sha and tokenHash, pending: true); after start returns, write the handle with a second update that does not require an unchanged rev (the slot is supervisor-owned). ADOPT BEFORE RELEASING: a pending slot or a queued run with no handle older than the start timeout is checked for its minted session (cli/cmux: <account dir>/sessions/*.json and the transcript; dorkos: GET /api/sessions/<id>); found -> adopt it into the slot; not found -> clear the slot (release a queued worker's claim to ready), EXCEPT when the host is dorkos and the launch went through session_start (server-minted id, so not found proves nothing): park the run with 'the supervisor stopped while starting a DorkOS session; check DorkOS for a session in <worktree> whose context names flow id <minted id>, then flow release or re-run'. Tests: a report landing mid-pass drops the decision but the launched reviewer's handle is still recorded and no second reviewer starts next pass; a crash after start and before recording is adopted, not released (no second worker in the worktree); on dorkos via session_start a not-found pending slot parks rather than releases. (4) fill slots: launchBudget({ load1: os.loadavg()[0], cpus: os.availableParallelism(), live, parallel, maxLoadPerCpu }) then S1 next logic with account assignment (task 3.1), filtered and ordered by --items; for each pick with an account: mint a UUID, provision the worktree, render the worker brief, claim with status queued (add an internal queued option to S1's claim function), launcher.start (worker, model = models.bindings[models.tiers.implementation], permission mode = flag, else drain.permissionMode), then set status running with the handle's sessionId, workerPid (pid or -1 for dorkos), account, host and drain = { v:1, phase:'working', worker: handle, ... }; on a start error release the claim to ready with the resume stage and report it. A pick with no account is skipped with the 'no account may take work' line. Reviewer launches (start-reviewer actions): git fetch origin <branch>, `git worktree add --detach <dorkHome>/workspaces/<repo>/review-<identifier>-<sha7> <sha>`, render the reviewer brief there, pick the account with rankAccounts (no affinity), model = models.bindings[models.tiers.review], start with role reviewer, record drain.reviewer { ...handle, sha, worktree }; remove the review worktree after its verdict or when it is stopped. (5) print one line per changed run; --json { v, runs: [{ identifier, phase, account, host, event }] }. WORKTREE (worktree.ts): path <dorkHome>/workspaces/<repo name>/<branch>, branch <identifier>-<slug> (title lowercased, runs of non-alphanumerics to '-', trimmed, at most 40 chars); git fetch origin then `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> origin/<default branch>`; reuse an existing worktree on that branch. BRIEFS (briefs.ts): render(templatePath, vars) replacing {{name}}; any unresolved {{...}} throws. Rewrite templates/drain/worker-brief.md as a template (vars identifier, title, worktree, branch, flow, accountLabel, rubric): keep its phases but replace hand steps with verbs (flow checkpoint --trigger task after each task commit; flow report pushed after each push, then stop and wait for a message; flow pr when told; flow report blocked for a question; closing-work then flow done when told the PR merged; flow stage --checkpoint-file at stage boundaries); remove 'claim' and any gh pr create step. Rewrite templates/drain/reviewer-brief.md (vars identifier, sha, base, deltaFrom sentence, rubric, flow, findingsFile): the reviewer is already in its detached worktree; it ends with flow report <id> verdict --sha <sha> --token <token> (--clean | --changes --findings-file <file>) (vars also include token). Keep every existing judgment rule in both briefs. RECOVERY: scripts/recovery.ts and the recovery step in skills/flow-drain/SKILL.md and commands/flow.md skip every run with drain set (a cli worker exits after each -p turn and a dorkos worker has workerPid -1, so pid-based orphan detection would resume a session the supervisor manages: two writers in one worktree); test that recovery ignores a drain run with a dead pid. VERIFYING-WORK: in a drain run (the worker brief says so) the worker skips verifying-work's own review and PR steps, runs flow report pushed and waits; edit skills/verifying-work/SKILL.md to say so in one line. STATUS: change S1's flow status drift check so runs with drain set use launcher.state instead of workerPid liveness, and show phase, account and host per drain run. SCHEDULED TICK: in skills/flow-drain/SKILL.md, the dispatch step runs `flow drain --tick` when drain.parallel >= 1 and keeps today's in-session path at 0; delete prose the verb replaces. tasks.subject: [flow-handoff-dispatch] [P4] Write the handoff state machine as a pure reducer
tasks.description: Depends on tasks 1.1 (synthesizeCheckpoint), 1.2 (limitSignal, rankAccounts) and 1.3 (RunLimit). Add scripts/drain/handoff.ts (zero deps) exporting nextHandoffAction({ run, signal, session, checkpoint, policy: { handoff: 'auto'|'ask' }, candidates (rankAccounts result with exclude [run.account] and no affinity), now, cfg: { windDownGraceMinutes } }) -> { run, actions }. signal is the worse of limitSignal over the run account's ledger and the worker's launcher state (limited counts as exhausted); the ambient account (account null) uses launcher state alone. Actions: { kind: 'send', message: 'wind-down'|'limit-cleared' } | { kind: 'synthesize-checkpoint', reason } | { kind: 'handoff', to, reason: 'warning'|'rejected'|'reset'|'manual' } | { kind: 'notify', candidate } | { kind: 'restart-reviewer' } | { kind: 'none' }. Implement exactly: (none) + warning -> limit { level warning, account: run.account, window, resetsAt, cause, since: now, state winding-down, notifiedAt null }, send wind-down ('finish the step you are on, commit, run flow checkpoint <id> --trigger limit-warning, report any push, then stop and take no new step on this account'). (none) + exhausted -> limit { level exhausted, state awaiting-handoff }. winding-down + signal ok -> clear limit; when the worker is idle or exited send limit-cleared. winding-down + exhausted -> awaiting-handoff. winding-down + a limit-warning checkpoint with writtenAt after since + worker idle or exited -> awaiting-handoff. winding-down + worker idle or exited + no such checkpoint + now - since >= grace -> synthesize-checkpoint then awaiting-handoff. awaiting-handoff + no checkpoint newer than since -> synthesize-checkpoint first (same pass continues). awaiting-handoff + auto + candidates.pick -> handoff(pick, reason warning or rejected by level), clear limit. awaiting-handoff + ask + pick -> pending-approval, notify(pick) once (set notifiedAt; never again this episode). awaiting-handoff + no pick -> waiting-reset with drain.wakeAfter = earliest resetsAt among this account's exhausted window and every candidate ineligible for limited or near-limit; none known -> now + 30 min. pending-approval + own account signal ok -> clear, send limit-cleared to the same session (reason reset; resuming on the same account needs no approval). waiting-reset + now >= wakeAfter + own ok -> clear, limit-cleared (reset). waiting-reset + now >= wakeAfter + a pick -> as awaiting-handoff (auto hands off, ask notifies). handing-off older than the start timeout (the mover died) -> if a session with limit.handoffSessionId exists, adopt it and finish the handoff (rewrite account, host, sessionId, handoffs, clear limit); else back to awaiting-handoff with handoffToken cleared, except onto dorkos via session_start where not-found parks (action { kind: 'adopt-or-revert-handoff' }); test it. A reviewer session that is limited -> restart-reviewer (stop it, new reviewer at the same SHA on another account), no RunLimit. The same machine applies when cause is reserve. TESTS engine-tests/drain/handoff.test.ts: every row in both auto and ask; a warning that clears before handoff; both synthesize paths; ask notifies exactly once per episode and again for a new episode; waiting-reset wakeAfter picks the earliest reset; limited reviewer restarts; the ambient account uses launcher state only. Validation (DOR-2374): a hard limit mid-item hands off with no operator action in auto; in ask the run parks and says why. (DOR-2371): the warning path is tested. Tracker: DOR-2374. tasks.subject: [flow-handoff-dispatch] [P4] Tell a live worker about a warning between tool calls: the limit-check hook
tasks.description: Depends on S1 (spec flow-cli-core, PR dork-labs/marketplace#53) being merged: scripts/flow.ts main(argv, deps) with its verb registry, --json envelope and exit codes (0 ok, 1 check found problems, 2 usage, 3 config, 4 tracker, 5 precondition, 6 missing zod, 7 paused); scripts/atomic-json.ts; scripts/flow-state-file.ts; scripts/fleet/accounts.ts (readIdentities, readFleetPolicy, mayServe, effectiveReservePct, fiveHourRoom, weeklyRoom, dorkHome resolution: DORK_HOME non-empty else os home/.dork); scripts/fleet/usage-ledger.ts (readLedger, readWindow, mergeLedger and the locked writer); config-load.ts; the code adapter (applyWorkState, comment, getItem); the claim/release/stage/done verbs. Also depends on task 1.2 (limitSignal). FIRST confirm against the installed Claude Code (record `claude --version` in the PR) that a PostToolUse command hook printing {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PostToolUse","additionalContext":"..."}} reaches the model; if it does not, ship only the verb (for manual use) without the hooks.json entry and say so in the PR: the supervisor's wind-down message (task 4.1) is then the only path. Add scripts/cli/limit-check.ts: `flow limit-check --hook` reads the hook stdin JSON (session_id, cwd); resolves the main checkout of cwd (parent of git rev-parse --git-common-dir) and reads .dork/flow/flow-state.json; finds the run whose sessionId equals session_id; computes limitSignal for the run's account from S1 readLedger/readWindow and readFleetPolicy (model from models.bindings[models.tiers.implementation] when config loads without zod, else null); when warning or exhausted and .dork/flow/drain/limit-notified-<sessionId>.json does not already hold the same { window, resetsAt }, prints the hookSpecificOutput JSON with the wind-down text (the same words as the wind-down message, with the flow command prefix) and writes the marker. Silent (no output) when: no run matches (a session outside flow), the account is ambient, no ledger, any error at all. Always exit 0. It must not import zod, call the tracker or the network, or take more than about 100 ms (it reads two small files). Also `flow limit-check <identifier>` (no --hook) prints the signal for manual use. Add to plugins/flow/hooks/hooks.json a PostToolUse entry running `node --experimental-strip-types "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/flow.ts" limit-check --hook` beside the existing Stop entry. tasks.subject: [flow-handoff-dispatch] [P4] Hand work off on a limit: flow handoff, ask-mode notice, and the runner wiring
tasks.description: Depends on tasks 3.5 (runner) and 4.1 (reducer). HANDOFF EXECUTION (scripts/drain/runner.ts, shared by the runner and the verb): (0) ONE HANDOFF AT A TIME: under the flow-state lock, compare-and-set limit.state = 'handing-off' with a fresh handoffToken, handingOffAt = now and handoffSessionId = the id it will mint, conditioned on run.sessionId still equal to the old session (a run with no limit gets a limit record with state handing-off for a manual move); if the CAS fails, stop (another handoff is in progress); if starting the new session fails, set state back to awaiting-handoff and clear the token. (1) ensure a checkpoint newer than limit.since exists, else write synthesizeCheckpoint(prev, facts) with facts from git (log since prev.headSha, at most 20 lines) and the reason; (2) launcher.stop(old worker) (cli/cmux stop the recorded pid; dorkos leaves it idle) so one writer per worktree holds; (3) host = the run's host; if its probe fails, do not hand off: park the run with the probe's reason (switching hosts would be a guess) and reset the handing-off state; (4) start a new worker on the target account, same cwd, first message resume-from-handoff ('You are continuing <id> in this worktree (<path>), on branch <branch>. Read .dork/flow/HANDOFF.md, then your brief at .dork/flow/drain/briefs/worker.md, then run the command under Next command. The previous session was on another account; do not run flow claim, the run is already yours.'), same model and permission mode; (5) rewrite FlowRun account, host, sessionId, workerPid (pid or -1), drain.worker; append drain.handoffs { from, to, at, reason }; clear limit; leave provenance untouched and the phase unchanged. It never reads or writes any account's projects/ directory. RUNNER: call nextHandoffAction before drainStep each pass and apply its actions (send via launcher.send; synthesize-checkpoint; handoff as above; restart-reviewer = stop reviewer + start a new one at the same SHA on another account; notify = once per episode, a signed comment through S1's adapter: '<account label> reached its <window label> limit (resets <local time>). This run is waiting. To continue on <candidate label> now, run `flow handoff <id> --to <candidate>`. Otherwise it continues here when the limit resets.' with no label change). Print the handoff and waiting lines ('<id> moved to <acct> (<window> limit on <old> until <time>)', '<id> limited until <time>, waiting for approval to move to <acct>'). S1 flow status shows the same waiting line for such runs. VERB scripts/cli/handoff.ts: `flow handoff <identifier> [--to <account-id>] [--reason <text>]`: --to must be eligible under rankAccounts with the run's account excluded, else exit 5 with its reasons; without --to take the pick (none -> exit 5 with reasons); refuse (exit 5) while a live flow drain holds drain.lock and the run is not limited; otherwise run the handoff with reason manual. TESTS extend engine-tests/drain/runner.test.ts (fake launcher, fake forge, fake adapter, temp repo, temp DORK_HOME, a fake fs layer that records every path read or written): AUTO: flip the worker account's fake ledger to rejected mid-item; the next pass writes a synthesized checkpoint, stops the old session, starts a new one on the other rotation account with cwd = the same worktree and the resume message, rewrites FlowRun.account/host/sessionId, appends handoffs, with no operator call. ASK: the same flip posts exactly one comment naming the candidate and the command and starts nothing; a second pass posts nothing more; then flow handoff moves it; separately, the account's reset (ledger resetsAt passes) resumes the same session with limit-cleared. WARNING: a ledger at allowed_warning sends wind-down; a limit-warning checkpoint plus an idle worker hands off proactively. NO TRANSCRIPT: across all cases the recorded fs paths include nothing under any account's projects/ directory. a failed host probe parks the run with the probe's reason and starts nothing; flow handoff: ineligible --to exits 5 with reasons; refused while a live drain holds the lock for a non-limited run; the supervisor and flow handoff racing on one limited run produce exactly one new session (the CAS loser starts nothing). Validation (DOR-2374): a hard limit mid-item hands off with no operator action in auto mode; in ask mode the run parks and says why; no transcript is moved automatically. Tracker: DOR-2374.
